title: Interactive AI assistance system for wound care: Integration of eNose, image recognition, and a chatbot for the early prediction of complications and to reduce the workload on nurses
summary:
Chronic wounds impair people’s quality of life. Those affected have a higher mortality rate. Approximately 1.8 million people in Germany have a chronic wound. The economic burden is enormous due to the prolonged course of the condition and the high level of care required. The documentation and management of these chronic wounds by nurses is labour-intensive and can lead to errors.
The IKIAWu research project is developing a technical system for the management of chronic wounds. This system will be installed on a mobile device, such as a tablet or iPad. The system is to be trained using artificial intelligence for wound recognition and management. The training will be carried out using photographs of wounds and swabs taken from the wound, which are normally taken in hospital in the case of a chronic wound. In addition, the system is trained using medical and nursing guidelines, as well as scientific evidence underpinning specialist knowledge on the treatment of chronic wounds.
Once the system has been developed, it will be trialled in hospital. To this end, the trained device will be used on patients with chronic wounds in addition to standard wound care and documentation. The aim is to investigate whether the system recognises the type of wound in the same way as nurses or doctors do. Furthermore, the predicted bacterial species will be compared with the laboratory results. The recommendations for wound treatment will be checked by nurses and doctors to ensure their accuracy.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Partial study 1 (retrospective study) Design and AI model development:
• All available image files of identified wounds as described: Condition/health problem under investigation
• Wound swabs taken as part of routine care and bacteriological laboratory cultures

Partial study 2 (prospective study) Development and piloting of the demonstrator:
• Inpatient or outpatient care
• Capacity to give consent or legal representation
• At least one chronic wound
Exclusion criteria:
Partial study 1 (retrospective study) Design and AI model development:
• insufficient image quality
• wound not fully captured
• multiple wound types
• personal characteristics (e.g. tattoos)

Partial study 2 (prospective study) Development and piloting of the demonstrator:
• Healed wounds
• Non-German-speaking patients
